description: Run SQL on any ADO.NET connection and get the rows back as strongly typed objects (ExecuteQuery<T>, ExecuteQueryAsync<T>) or as dynamic objects (ExecuteQuery, ExecuteQueryAsync), streamed as IEnumerable<T> or IAsyncEnumerable<T>. The methods extend DbConnection and DbCommand; ExecuteCommand and ExecuteCommandAsync run statements that return no rows. An error the database raises after the rows (SQL Server THROW after a SELECT) is thrown when the rows are read to their end. Parameters are written as {{name}} in the SQL and always sent as real database parameters, never concatenated into it. Their names can hold any characters, so a JSON body's keys work as they are ({{first name}}, {{e-mail}}); names are matched ignoring case, and a name the parameters object lacks, or whose value is null, is sent as NULL. Their values come from an anonymous object, a dictionary, a JsonElement or JSON text, and the delimiters can be changed. Several parameter sources, each with its own delimiters, can fill one query, a later source taking precedence. Typed results map columns to properties by name, or by [DataMember] or [JsonPropertyName]. JSON and XML columns can be returned as nested objects. Works with SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, SQLite, Oracle, DB2 and any other ADO.NET provider; on ODBC and OleDb the named parameters become positional ? parameters automatically. No package dependencies on .NET 8 and later. Targets .NET 10, 9 and 8, and .NET Standard 2.0, which includes .NET Framework 4.6.1 and later.
releaseNotes: Fill fills placeholders by the rules the query methods bind them with, and every parameter source keeps its place. 1) One name under two markers of one pattern ({{id}} and {j{id}}, under a pattern that accepts both) gets its value at every marker. Only the first marker found used to be filled: the other was left as text, emptied, or filled from a set the list ranks lower. 2) Fill inserts a value once and never reads it again: placeholder text inside a value ({{other}}, or another set's marker such as {s{key}}) stays as it is. It used to be filled again, by its own set or by a set listed before it (the sets are applied last to first), or emptied by the null replacement. So a value someone else supplied could pull in another set's value (a secret, say) that the template never placed there, and a value holding an open marker could swallow the placeholder after it. 3) With several sets, the latest set in the list with a non-null value fills a placeholder, whatever order the markers are written in. 4) caseSensitive: true also replaces case-sensitively: {{NAME}} is no longer filled from a name value. 5) With a one-marker pattern (:name), a name that goes on from another name (:date_from, or :date-from under a pattern that allows "-") keeps its own value, null included, on every path, where the shorter name's pattern matches it as a longer placeholder somewhere in the text (one that skips that spot, with a lookbehind, gives the named path and Fill the shorter name's value there). Fill used to give it the shorter name's value, and so did the named-parameter path for :date-from under a pattern that allows "-", when it was null or its value came from a set listed before the shorter name's. A pattern with no open_marker and close_marker groups has Fill replace only its matches, not the bare name everywhere. 6) valueConverter is called once per name and source, not once per marker or spelling: {{id}}, {j{id}} and {{ID}} from one source make one call. 7) A null entry in a list of DbQueryParams is skipped by Fill, ReduceToUnique and the query methods. It used to throw NullReferenceException. 8) On every path, a pattern no longer reads into a placeholder that a set read before it has already replaced. A pattern that can match digits or symbols (\d+, \w+, [^\w\s]) used to throw FormatException or lose a value there, and a stray open marker that paired with a close marker past such a placeholder made the text between them one placeholder: Fill dropped that text, and the query methods bound it as one NULL. On the named-parameter path and in Fill, the placeholder whose close marker the stray marker takes is still filled where the pattern matches it on its own in the text as written; on the named-parameter path only when it has a value, as a NULL placeholder is replaced only where its pattern matches it. 9) Fill throws ArgumentException for text that contains every private-use character (U+E000 to U+F8FF) whenever it is given parameters, as the query methods do: one is needed to mark placeholders while they are resolved. Finding it takes one pass over the text. With no parameters (null) or an empty list it returns the text as it is, as before; the query methods throw for an empty list. 10) A source's values no longer move past the sources listed between it and a later source with the exact same pattern string, on any path. Such sources are read as one, in the place of the last of them, and a placeholder used to take the earlier one's value even over a source listed between them (a body source listed before a query-string source beat it when a third source shared the body's pattern). They are still read as one, a later one's value for a name deciding even when it is null, but a source listed between them that has a value for the name, and whose pattern reads that placeholder where it is written, now takes it: with both markers, every use of its text, as that source's own pass would; with one marker or none, only the uses the shared pattern matches there too, as the text stands when it reads it: a use it recovers from the text as written after a stray marker (item 8) keeps the earlier source's value, also where 10.1.0.11 gave it the source listed between. Where its pattern reads a longer or shorter placeholder at that spot (:x-1 against :x), the earlier source's value is used, as before: give the sources different pattern strings then. It binds the plain spelling of its spaced placeholder ({{id}} for {{ id }}) only where its own pass still has that placeholder, or where the sources that share the pattern have a value for that spelling. On ODBC and OleDb, where only the patterns' matches are replaced, it also takes nothing where another source with a value has a placeholder that overlaps one of its pattern's matches without being the same one (a stray {{ paired past one), if that source is listed after it and the last source with that source's exact pattern string is listed no later than the last of the two that share the pattern. 11) A pattern that allows text between a marker and the name ({{ name }} under (?<open_marker>\{\{)\s*(?<param>\w+)\s*(?<close_marker>\}\})) has a placeholder with a value replaced on every path. Fill used to leave it as written, and the query methods on named-parameter providers left it in the SQL (ODBC and OleDb already replaced it). Its plain spelling ({{name}}) is bound too, where the pattern also takes that for a placeholder of the name.
